newsitem.title: USA: College poll shows Clinton with 34-point lead.
newsitem.headline: College poll shows Clinton with 34-point lead.

text.p: President Clinton enjoys a commanding 34-point lead over Republican challenger Bob Dole in a new poll of 46,509 college students released on Friday.
The poll was conducted Oct. 23 by Follett College Stores, which manages 500 U.S. college bookstores, at special electronic pollling stations.
In the poll, Clinton won 61.3 percent of the vote, compared to just 27.1 percent for Dole. Reform Party candidate Ross Perot got 7.1 percent of the vote, faring better than in most national polls.

Not surprisingly, educational funding and support was a main issue of concern for 54.4 percent of the college students, while wage and tax policies rated 37 percent and the job market rated 33.9 percent.
Over 70 percent of the students polled were registered voters.

Meanwhile, the music television cable network MTV said it would host five hours of live political programming on Saturday, Nov. 2, as part of its "Choose or Lose '96" campaign to encourage voter turnout on Election Day, Nov. 5.
